messages.subject: Convergence diagnostics
messages.body_plain:
I have just started learning to use 'nimble'. It looks like a very useful addition to the current softwares on hierarchical models and MCMC. Thanks for developing this. Now to my questions (naive, almost certainly):

1) How do I run several chains to see if I have convergence and mixing? I can write a do loop, I guess. But is there a simple option such as n.chains in JAGS? Is there a simple way to get different diagnostics or do I have to feed the output to CODA to get it?

2) If I have new data set, do I have to recompile the model with the new data?

Thanks, Perry and colleagues, for your wonderful work.

Subhash

messages.subject: Re: Convergence diagnostics
messages.body_plain:
Hi Subhash,

Nice to see you here and thanks for the message.

1. No, it is of course a minor point but we have not automated the running of multiple chains.  Yes, feeding the output to CODA makes sense.  In MCMCsuite (and compareMCMC, a higher level version in upcoming 0.5 release soon) we use coda::effectiveSize to estimate the effective sample size, but we don’t otherwise access coda tools automatically.

2. No, you can just assign the data to the appropriate variables in the model.

For example

myCode <- nimbleCode({ ## world’s simplest model
  mu ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  y ~ dnorm(mu, 1)
})

myModel <- nimbleModel(myCode, data = list(y = 1.23))

CmyModel <- compileNimble(myModel)
CmyModel$y  ## should be 1.23, the value you happened to set at model definition
CmyModel$y <- 2.34 ## now it has a new value
## if you want to simulate data, you must provide includeData = TRUE to the simulate function
## otherwise it will respect data labels and not overwrite values in those nodes
CmyModel$mu <- 0.5 ## need a value here for simulation of y to produce something meaningful
simulate(CmyModel, ‘y’, includeData = TRUE)
calculate(CmyModel) ## update logProbs if needed

Best
Perry

messages.subject: my_RW code (page 88 of the manual)
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys:

I was looking at this example code because I want to write my own proposal distribution keeping everything else as is. If I understand correctly the command:

proposal <- norm(1,model[[target]],scale)

can be changed to any distribution. For example, if I have multiple target nodes, it can be a multivariate normal distribution of dimension equal to the number  of random effects plus the number of hyper-parameters. Or, some other distribution can be used here as long as it has the correct dimension.

There are two questions:

a) Does it have to be one of the standard distributions or can I use something else such as mixtures of normals say or product of gamma distribution for one parameter and mixture of univariate normal distributions for the other hyper parameters?

b) The acceptance probability depends on the form of the proposal distribution and not just the distribution of the random effects and hyper parameters. But the Metropolis step described later in the function seems to not have proposal distribution density.

I am sure I am missing something obvious. I am not too facile in computing. Thanks for your help.

Subhash Lele

messages.subject: Re: my_RW code (page 88 of the manual)
messages.body_plain:
Subhash, thanks for your email.  I'm happy to see you're interested in writing your own sampler function in NIMBLE!  Please keep in touch with how it works, and any more questions you might have along the way.  Let me address your questions.

>> proposal <- norm(1,model[[target]],scale)
>> can be changed to any distribution. For example, if I have multiple target nodes, it can be a multivariate normal distribution of dimension equal to the number  of random effects plus the number of hyper-parameters. Or, some other distribution can be used here as long as it has the correct dimension.

Yes, exactly right.  You could use any multivariate distribution here (of the correct dimension), or any combination of values generated from different distributions.  In that case, you could individually add elements of the proposal vector (e.g., proposal[1:k] ) one at a time, or in blocks:
proposal[1:3] <- ....
proposal[4] <- .....
etc..

>> a) Does it have to be one of the standard distributions or can I use something else such as mixtures of normals say or product of gamma distribution for one parameter and mixture of univariate normal distributions for the other hyper parameters?

No, it does not need to be one of the standard distributions.  Yes, you could use a mixture of normal distributions.  If you want the mixture distribution to vary (i.e. not be fixed), then you could use other model nodes to define properties of the mixture distribution.  In that case, the control list argument can be used to supply the model node names which defined properties of the mixture.

>> b) The acceptance probability depends on the form of the proposal distribution and not just the distribution of the random effects and hyper parameters. But the Metropolis step described later in the function seems to not have proposal distribution density.

Correct.  The example shown doesn't include the proposal density since it's a symmetric normal distribution.  To correctly implement your sampler, you would have to calculate the forward and backward proposal densities (which can use calls to standard R density functions, i.e. dgamma()), then include this additive terms in the MH ratio calculation:
log_MH_ratio <- model_lp_proposed - model_lp_initial + backward_proposal_logdensity - forward_proposal_logdensity
(forgive me if I have the +/- signs wrong)

Good luck!  Let us know if you have other questions.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.subject: Re: compileNimble error from r-nimble.org's example
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ed,

Sorry to hear this is giving you the runaround.

It sounds like something is not fully installed correctly.  These can be hard for us to diagnose, but I think it has to do with your compiler and related tools (see Ch. 4 in our User Manual if you haven’t looked at that yet).  Here are some suggestions of issues we’ve seen people run into.

On Windows, when installing Rtools.exe, there may be a check box to modify the PATH, which should be checked.

On Mac, when installing Xcode, the command line tools need to be included.  Also it may be necessary to launch Xcode once on its own before using it through nimble (it may take a password when first launched).

If you try reinstalling your C++ compiler based on the above points, you may then need to reinstall nimble.

Please let us know if you’re still stuck, and also let us know if one of these seems to solve your problem so we can amass experience about issues people are running into.

Thanks
Perry

messages.subject: Problems to install Nimble.
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm using Ubuntu 14.04 LTS, and  I've tried to install Nimble both from the website (install.packages("nimble", repos = "http://r-nimble.org") ) and from local file  by  using configure.args = "--with-eigen=/path/to/eigen" as suggested in the user manual (btw, the former method solved a problem with Eigen/Dense file  ( "Cannot find Eigen/Dense include file.") I had found when  trying to install from the webpage.

Anyway, in both cases the process (from local file and from the Nimble website) is stopped giving the following error message:

** R
** inst
** preparing package for lazy loading
Error in list2env(list(), NULL, <environment>) :
  names(x) must be a character vector of the same length as x
Error : unable to load R code in package ‘nimble’
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package ‘nimble’

I got sure all requirements (C++ compilers and others) are OK, and my R version is  3.0.2.

I found that somebody else had mentioned the same error when trying to install Nimble in a Mac some time ago ( https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/issues/99), but the solution suggested there didn't fix my problem.

As a remark, somebody else in my lab, using the same Ubuntu, got the same error message when trying to install the package.

I would really appreciate any suggestion or any hint to find out what is going wrong.

All the best,

Soledad

messages.subject: Re: Problems to install Nimble.
messages.body_plain:
As of Nimble v0.4, we introduced an (at the time) unrealized
dependency on R >= 3.1.2 because of an issue with list2env() in R <=
3.1.1. So installation of Nimble 0.4 and 0.4-1 won't work with R 3.1.1
or older.

In our upcoming Nimble 0.5 release, the dependency on R >= 3.1.2 will
be explicit.
